advances:
The prescribed common-middle calibration is infeasible for every convex
polygon, rational or otherwise.  In fact, containment of the fixed triangle
and the two prescribed side-cone areas alone force every point of \(K\) in
the open positive quadrant to satisfy \(x+y<1\).  The whole prescribed
positive-quadrant area would then lie in the prescribed strip, where it is
already too large.
author: r107_tail_six_cone_gluing
proof:
Write
\[
O=(0,0),\qquad A=(-p,0),\qquad B=(0,-q).
\]
Suppose first that \(Z=(X,Y)\in K\) has \(X>0\), \(Y>0\), and put
\(h=X+Y\).  Convexity and \(D\subseteq K\) imply
\[
\operatorname{conv}\{A,O,Z\}\subseteq K.
\]
The segment from \(A\) to \(Z\) meets the line \(x+y=0\) at
\[
W_A=
\left(-\frac{pY}{h+p},\frac{pY}{h+p}\right).
\]
Apart from its three boundary segments, the triangle
\(\operatorname{conv}\{A,O,W_A\}\) lies in
\(\{x<0,\ y>0,\ x+y<0\}\).  Its area is
\[
\frac12\left|\det(A,W_A)\right|
=\frac{p^2Y}{2(h+p)}.
\]
It follows from the prescribed area of that open cone that
\[
\frac{p^2Y}{2(h+p)}\le\frac1{2000},
\qquad\text{hence}\qquad
Y\le\frac{h+p}{1000p^2}.                                      \tag{1}
\]

Likewise,
\[
\operatorname{conv}\{B,O,Z\}\subseteq K,
\]
and the segment from \(B\) to \(Z\) meets \(x+y=0\) at
\[
W_B=
\left(\frac{qX}{h+q},-\frac{qX}{h+q}\right).
\]
Apart from its boundary, the triangle
\(\operatorname{conv}\{B,O,W_B\}\) lies in
\(\{x>0,\ y<0,\ x+y<0\}\), and its area is
\[
\frac12\left|\det(B,W_B)\right|
=\frac{q^2X}{2(h+q)}.
\]
Therefore
\[
X\le\frac{h+q}{1000q^2}.                                      \tag{2}
\]

If \(h\ge1\), then (1) and (2), together with \(X+Y=h\), give
\[
1
\le
\frac1{1000}
\left(
\frac1{p^2}+\frac1p+\frac1{q^2}+\frac1q
\right).
\]
But \(p>1\) and \(q>\tfrac12\), so
\[
\frac1{p^2}+\frac1p+\frac1{q^2}+\frac1q
<1+1+4+2=8.
\]
This would imply \(1<8/1000\), a contradiction.  Hence every point of
\(K\) in the open positive quadrant satisfies \(0<x+y<1\).

Thus, up to boundary sets of area zero,
\[
K\cap\{x>0,\ y>0\}
\subseteq K\cap\{0<x+y\le1\}.
\]
The two prescribed areas would consequently satisfy
\[
\frac{628}{2000}
\le\frac1{3000},
\]
whereas
\[
\frac{628}{2000}=\frac{157}{500}=\frac{942}{3000}
>\frac1{3000}.
\]
This contradiction proves the claimed nonexistence.  Since every polygon
in the registered problem contains \(D\) and has the four areas used above,
no such polygon exists.
statement:
Put
\[
p=\frac{174}{121},\qquad q=\frac{121}{200},
\]
and
\[
D=\operatorname{conv}\{(0,0),(-p,0),(0,-q)\}.
\]
There is no compact two-dimensional convex set \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^2\)
such that \(D\subseteq K\) and simultaneously
\[
\left|K\cap\{x<0,\ y>0,\ x+y<0\}\right|
=
\left|K\cap\{x>0,\ y<0,\ x+y<0\}\right|
=\frac1{2000},
\]
\[
\left|K\cap\{x>0,\ y>0\}\right|=\frac{628}{2000},
\]
and
\[
\left|K\cap\{0<x+y\le1\}\right|=\frac1{3000}.
\]
Consequently, no convex polygon satisfies all the conditions in the
registered fixed six-cone gluing problem.
